headline: Town boards advanced key Town Meeting articles this week, including school and municipal budgets, major school building projects, and an appointed clerk proposal.
synopsis: Southborough officials focused heavily on preparations for the April 11 Annual Town Meeting, with the Select Board tentatively endorsing a 4.88% municipal budget increase and the School Committee holding a public hearing on its $26.1 million operating budget. School leaders also approved bid specifications for the Neary Elementary School feasibility study and reviewed an $8.8 million roof replacement for Trottier Middle School that qualifies for partial state funding. Capital planners and town officials evaluated major borrowing proposals, including a $25 million authorization for road and sidewalk improvements. Additionally, the Conservation Commission opened hearings on a multi-family proposal under the MBTA Communities zoning overlay, and the joint school committees approved several updated district policies.

highlights.title: Select Board endorses FY27 budget and Town Meeting articles
highlights.why: The Select Board voted 3-1-1 to conditionally endorse an FY27 operating budget reflecting a 4.88% increase and leaving a $414,000 levy balance. Final votes on union contract figures, healthcare numbers, and major capital borrowing were deferred to March 17.

highlights.title: Trottier Middle School roof replacement project reviewed
highlights.why: The School Committee reviewed plans for an $8,833,964 roof replacement heading to Town Meeting as Article 15. The Massachusetts School Building Authority has approved a 41.32% grant covering roughly $3.4 million, leaving a net cost to Southborough of approximately $5.4 million subject to Town Meeting and ballot approval.

highlights.title: Neary School feasibility study bid document approved
highlights.why: Following approval of $175,000 at the March Special Town Meeting, the School Committee voted 4-0 to approve the Request for Services to hire an architect and engineer. The study will analyze comprehensive renovation options and evaluate deferred maintenance capped at $15 million less the cost of roof replacement.

highlights.title: Proposed $25 million borrowing for town roads and sidewalks
highlights.why: Capital planners and the town administrator reviewed a proposed $25 million multi-year borrowing authorization to address road and sidewalk infrastructure. Select Board members agreed that large-scale road and sidewalk debt should be separated into its own warrant article subject to a town-wide debt exclusion vote.

highlights.title: Proposal to make Town Clerk an appointed office
highlights.why: The Select Board voted 5-0 to support Article 25, which would convert the Town Clerk from an elected position to an appointed one. The change requires approval by Annual Town Meeting voters and a majority vote on the annual town election ballot.

highlights.title: MBTA overlay apartment development hearing opened
highlights.why: The Conservation Commission began reviewing a Notice of Intent and Stormwater Permit for two apartment buildings and a clubhouse on 4 acres at 0 Southville Road. Neighbors raised concerns regarding environmental impacts, fire access, and past site clearing, leading the commission to continue the hearing to April 30.
